title: Common Proxy Settings Summary
content:
Preface
Note: all examples below use dummy proxies; replace them with your own.

Proxies are set for these situations:

Crossing the GFW Great Firewall, abbreviated as 翻墙
Accessing 外网 from 内网
Accessing 内网镜像库 from 内网 (npm, composer, etc.)

 Proxy methods
There are at least the following ways to configure a proxy:


Set the target proxy machine (most common)

e.g.: http://yourProxyServer:port



Set a PAC file to match proxies automatically (common in browsers)

e.g.: http://example/a.pac



 Proxy address
Assume your currently available proxy is: http://yourProxyServer:port; the examples below all use this proxy.
 Windows CMD proxy settings
Effective for the current CMD window:
REM 设置代理
set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port
set https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

REM 查看代理
echo %http_proxy%
echo %https_proxy%

REM 取消代理(留空即可)
set http_proxy=
set https_proxy=
To make it permanent, set the system environment variables http_proxy and https_proxy, then restart Windows.
Notes:

http_proxy and https_proxy both correspond to http://yourProxyServer:port; the latter may not have the s of https.

 Linux proxy settings
Same as the Mac proxy settings below ↓
 Mac proxy settings
This section only covers configuring a proxy from the command line.
Add a shortcut for setting the proxy in ~/.bash_profile or ~/.zshrc:
# shadowsocks 翻墙用，不翻墙可不用
alias proxy_ss='export all_proxy=socks5://127.0.0.1:1086; export http_proxy=http://127.0.0.1:1087; export https_proxy=https://127.0.0.1:1087'

# 其他代理
alias proxy_dev='export http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port; export https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port'

# 取消所有代理设置
alias unproxy='unset all_proxy; unset http_proxy; unset https_proxy'
After setting it up, remember to source the config file.
To use it, run in the shell (using a dev machine as an example):
# 设置代理
proxy_dev

# 取消代理
unproxy

Standalone commands:
# 临时设置代理
export http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port
export https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

# 查看代理
echo $http_proxy
echo $https_proxy

# 取消代理
unset http_proxy
unset https_proxy
 Mac Homebrew proxy settings
Same as the Mac command-line proxy settings above.

Brew 官方参考

 Git proxy settings

Git

# 全局：设置 Git 访问外网（如 github）的代理
git config --global http.proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

# 全局：查看 Git 代理
git config --global --get http.proxy

# 全局：删除 Git 代理
git config --global --unset http.proxy



# ----------- 下面是针对每个项目局部的，非全局 -----------------
# 设置 Git 访问外网（如 github）的代理
git config http.proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

# 查看 Git 代理
git config --get http.proxy

# 删除 Git 代理
git config --unset http.proxy
 Git username and email settings
# 设置 Git 全局：用户名、邮箱 ↓
git config --global user.name "youName"
git config --global user.email yourEmail@example.com

# 下面是针对每个 Git 项目的，非全局 ↓
git config user.email yourEmail@example.com
git config user.name "youName"
Which one to set globally and which one for the current project depends on your needs; there is no absolute rule.
 npm proxy settings + registry settings

npm

 Using the Taobao npm mirror (recommended)
In this case you need to set both: the Taobao mirror + your proxy (if any)
# ↓ 设置淘宝 npm 镜像
npm config set registry https://registry.npmmirror.com
# ↓ 若本来即可访问外网，无需下面代理设置
npm config set https-proxy http://yourProxyServer:port
 Using the official npm registry
Set the proxy (if any):
npm config set proxy http://yourProxyServer:port
npm config set https-proxy http://yourProxyServer:port
 How to check npm proxy and registry settings
# 查看 npm 所有设置
npm config list

# 查看代理
npm config get proxy
npm config get https-proxy

# 查看镜像
npm config get registry

# 取消代理
npm config rm proxy
npm config rm https-proxy
 yarn proxy settings + registry settings

yarn

# 设置 registry 镜像
yarn config set registry https://registry.npmmirror.com

# 设置代理（若有的话）
yarn config set proxy http://yourProxyServer:port

# 查看所有设置
yarn config list

# 查看镜像设置
yarn config get registry

# 查看某个设置
yarn config get proxy
yarn global config: 用户目录/.yarnrc
Notes:


Sometimes the proxy still doesn’t take effect; this may be caused by a problem with the yarn.lock file — try deleting it and starting over.



Reference: yarnpkg/yarn#4890





 nvm proxy settings

nvm

# 设置代理（永久）
nvm proxy "http://yourProxyServer:port"

# 设置代理（临时，非必须）
set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port
set https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port

# 查看代理
nvm proxy

# 删除代理
nvm proxy "none"

Reference: https://github.com/coreybutler/nvm-windows#usage

 Bower proxy settings

Bower

Create a new .bowerrc file and fill in proxy and https-proxy:
{
  "directory": "bower_components",
  "proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port/",
  "https-proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port/"
}
Three placement options are supported:

Current project: 当前目录（bower.json 的同级目录）
Current user’s home directory
System root directory (the / directory on Linux)


Reference: https://bower.io/docs/config/#placement--order

 PHP Composer proxy settings

Composer

After installing Composer, Composer uses the system proxy directly (e.g., CMD on Windows); there is no proxy config file.
That is: on Windows you need to set the CMD proxy, something like
set http_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
set https_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
Only then can you run composer require packageName
If the system has these two environment variables configured, that effectively acts as Composer’s global proxy.
 PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, WebStorm, Android Studio (or other JetBrains IDEs) proxy settings

Jetbrains

File -> Settings -> Appearance & Behavior -> System Settings
-> HTTP Proxy -> Manual proxy configuration -> HTTP
-> Host name: yourProxyServer -> Port number: yourProxyPort
-> OK
 Maven proxy and mirror settings

Maven

Maven’s proxy and mirror settings are fairly extensive; see 这里 for details.
 Gradle proxy settings

Gradle


To configure for the current project:

Create or edit gradle.properties inside the current project


To configure globally:

Create or edit 用户目录/.gradle/gradle.properties



Add the following settings to the gradle.properties file:
systemProp.http.proxyHost=yourProxyServer
systemProp.http.proxyPort=yourPort
systemProp.https.proxyHost=yourProxyServer
systemProp.https.proxyPort=yourPort

Reference: https://docs.gradle.org/current/userguide/build_environment.html

 pip Proxy Settings for Python
pip is used to install Python packages.
There are 3 ways to set a proxy for pip (pick one):


System environment variables

Just like the CMD proxy settings, then pip install yourPackage, Win ↓

set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port
set https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port


--proxy parameter

pip install yourPackage --proxy http://yourProxyServer:port



pip.ini config file (recommended, permanent)


Taking Win as an example, create a new directory and file %HOME%\pip\pip.ini in your user directory, and fill in:
[install]
proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port


To check whether it worked: pip config list





Official pip documentation on setting a proxy: https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/user_guide/#using-a-proxy-server

 VS Code Proxy Settings
VSCode reads the proxy from the http_proxy and https_proxy environment variables by default.
But you can also set it manually: File -> Preference -> Settings, then paste the following code into User Settings on the right:
"http.proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",
 Notepad++ Proxy Settings

Notepad++

Menu bar -> question mark ? on the far right -> 设置更新代理服务器 ->

Proxy server: yourProxyServer
Port: yourPort

 Sublime Proxy Settings
Sublime uses the system’s PAC settings by default. If your browser can get online, Sublime basically can too.
You can also customize the proxy in the config file:

菜单栏 -> Preferences -> Settings -> 在左右任意一侧填入:

"http_proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",
"https_proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",
 Eclipse Proxy Settings
Ways to set a proxy for Eclipse:

Window -> Preferences -> General -> Network Connections -> select Manual in Active Provider on the right -> double-click HTTP on line 1 under Proxy entries 表格 -> enter yourProxyServer in Host -> enter yourPort in Port -> OK
Set HTTPS and SOCKS the same way

 Atom Editor Proxy Settings

Atom

See the commands below:
# 设置代理
apm config set https-proxy https://yourProxyServer:port

# 查看代理
apm config get https-proxy

# 查看所有配置（显示的结果的 `userconfig` 就是配置文件所在位置）
apm config get

Reference: https://github.com/atom/apm#using-a-proxy

 wget Proxy Settings

wget Win
wget Linux

Method 01 (temporary):


First set the proxy in Windows CMD:
set http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port
set https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port


Or the proxy in a Linux shell:
export http_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port
export https_proxy=http://yourProxyServer:port


Then you can use the wget command directly


Method 02 (permanent, recommended!):


Just use the wget config file: create a new file .wgetrc in the current user’s home directory (or /etc/wgetrc on Linux):
http-proxy = yourProxyServer:port
https-proxy = yourProxyServer:port
ftp-proxy = yourProxyServer:port


Then you can use the wget command directly


Method 03 (temporary):

Add parameters directly to the wget command, e.g.

wget https://www.baidu.com -e https-proxy=yourProxyServer:port
or (both are http, not https)
wget http://www.baidu.com -e http-proxy=yourProxyServer:port



 curl Proxy Settings

curl

Method 01 (temporary):
(This is part 2 of 4 of the same post.)

First, set the proxy for Windows CMD:set http_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
set https_proxy=yourProxyServer:port

Or the proxy for the Linux shell:export http_proxy=yourProxyServer:port
export https_proxy=yourProxyServer:port

Then you can use the curl command directly, for example

curl http://www.baidu.com -o baidu.html



Method 02 (permanent, recommended!):

Just use the curl config file. Create a new config file in the current user’s home directory (Win: _curlrc) (Linux: .curlrc):proxy = yourProxyServer:port

Then you can use the curl command directly, for example

curl http://www.baidu.com -o baidu.html



Method 03 (temporary):

Add the parameter directly to the curl command, for example

curl https://www.baidu.com -o baidu.html -x yourProxyServer:port

-x The lowercase x means proxy





 Golang’s go get Proxy
Golang’s go get uses the system’s http_proxy, but pulling code uses Git’s proxy,
so you need to do both steps:

Set the system proxy (or CMD proxy)

set http_proxy=yourProxyServer:port

Set the Git proxy, see Git 代理设置 above

git config --global http.proxy http://yourProxyServer:port
References:

https://stackoverflow.com/a/10385612/2752670
Official reference: https://github.com/golang/go/wiki/GoGetProxyConfig

If you use VS Code, and want VS Code to automatically download Go’s dependency tools, you should also set the proxy in VS Code’s settings.json:
"http.proxy": "http://yourProxyServer:port",
 Navicat Connecting to an External Database
Navicat seemingly requires configuring both 通道地址 and 代理服务器.
Note: This method is not very secure; use it with caution!

Step 01: In the Navicat installation directory, find the file: C:\Program Files\PremiumSoft\Navicat Premium\ntunnel_mysql.php (or the php for the corresponding language), and place it in your external web service directory (open http://IP:port/abc/ntunnel_mysql.php in a browser and you should see a page)
Step 02: 右键某个数据库连接 -> HTTP -> check 使用 HTTP 通道 -> fill in http://IP:port/abc/ntunnel_mysql.php for 通道地址 -> below 代理服务器 -> check 使用代理服务器 -> fill in yourPorxyServer for 主机 -> fill in yourPort for 端口 -> 测试连接 -> 确定

 VirtualBox and VMware Proxy Settings
Most users run their VMs in NAT mode.
Proxy settings: the system inside the VM must use the same proxy settings as the host physical machine in order to get online.
 Xshell Proxy Settings
Open the properties of a session

Connection
Proxy
Browse
Add

Name: anyName (or any name you like)
Type: HTTP 1.1
Host: yourProxyServer
Port: yourPort
OK
Close


For Proxy Server, select the proxy you just created
Done

 SecureCRT Proxy Settings
Two steps: first add a global proxy entry, then select the corresponding proxy entry in each connection.

Add a global proxy entry


Options
Global Options
Firewall

Add

Name: anyName (or any name you like)
Type: HTTP (no authentication)
Hostname or IP: yourProxyServer
Port: yourPort
OK






Select the newly created proxy entry in your connection


Your connection -> Properties
Connection
SSH2
Firewall
Select 刚新建的代理项

 Proxifier: Setting Up a Proxy for Other Software

Proxifier

Unlike the previous software, where each sets its own proxy, Proxifier takes a different approach: it sets up a proxy for other software uniformly.
Advantages:

No need to configure proxies separately for each app in its own way
Apps without a proxy settings UI work well with Proxifier
You can see the actual traffic of the proxied apps
Works on both Windows and Mac

Drawbacks:

Proxy settings aren’t always granular enough (e.g., Git’s global proxy vs. the proxy for the current Git project)

Steps:

菜单栏 Profile -> Proxy Servers -> Add -> Address, enter yourProxyServer -> Port, enter yourPort -> Protocol, enter HTTPS -> OK
菜单栏 Profile -> Proxification Rules -> Add -> Name, fill in anything - > Applications select the exe file of the app you want to proxy via the Browse button -> Action choose the yourProxyServer set in the previous steps -> OK

 Credits
Thanks to Dylan for the proxy roundup!

This article is reposted from: dylan-7/note/blob/main/常用代理设置汇总.md

title: Deploying Meting-API
content:
This tutorial uses the xizeyoupan/Meting-API open-source project on GitHub to deploy your own serverless Meting-API
This article is mainly aimed at those without a server; if you have one, you can switch to this repository metowolf/Meting-API for deployment
Benefits of self-hosting: no one else controls your API calls, and there’s no risk of the service shutting down, because the API is in your own hands
Demo Test: meting-api.saop.cc/test


 Prerequisites

Register a GitHub account (skip this if you already have one)
Register a Vercel account (skip this if you already have one)
Have a tool that can access the GitHub and Vercel websites (a VPN)
A domain of your own and some basic computer knowledge
A pair of hands, a brain, a pair of eyes, and a computer or phone

 Tutorial
 0x0001
Go to the repository of the xizeyoupan/Meting-API open-source project, click the Fork button in the top right corner to fork the main branch of this repository,
Go to the Vercel platform and click Add New... > Project, use your brain a little, and add the repository you just forked,
 0x0002
After the deployment succeeds, go to the project’s Settings > Domains custom domains, add your own subdomain, like mine meting-api.saop.cc
Go to your domain’s DNS provider (for example, Tencent Cloud for my domain) and add the CNAME record provided by Vercel
 0x0003
Wait a bit, about two or three minutes, then visit the domain you just bound 二级域名/test, for example https://meting-api.saop.cc/test
If you get an error, start over from the beginning; it’s usually a mistake in your own operations. If it succeeds, the following test page will appear:

The top left of each song shows the provider and the retrieved type, corresponding to:



Original name
Provider
Type




tencent playlist
QQ Music
Playlist


tencent song
QQ Music
Track


netease playlist
NetEase Cloud Music
Playlist


netease song
NetEase Cloud Music
Track


netease artist
NetEase Cloud Music
Artist


ytmusic playlist
YouTube
Playlist


ytmusic song
YouTube
Track


spotify playlist
Spotify
Playlist


spotify song
Spotify
Track



If some provider or type is blank, it means data can’t be retrieved for that provider or type, so avoid that option when using it
 Usage
 API Parameters


server: data source

netease: NetEase Cloud Music
tencent: QQ Music



type: type

name: song name
artist: artist
url: link
pic: cover
lrc: lyrics
song: track
playlist: playlist



id: the ID for the type (cover ID / track ID / playlist ID)


For example:

https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=netease&type=url&id=416892104
https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=netease&type=song&id=591321
https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=netease&type=playlist&id=2619366284



 Embedding the API in Meting.min.js
Save the Meting.min.js file to your own device

Meting.min.js: https://npm.elemecdn.com/meting/dist/Meting.min.js

Edit this file, press Ctrl + F to search for api?server=, replace https://api.i-meto.com/meting/api?server= with your own API, then press Ctrl + S to save

Before: https://api.i-meto.com/meting/api?server=
After: https://meting-api.saop.cc/api?server=

Once you’ve replaced it, you can put it in your code space and reference this file via a link, or place it locally and reference it with a relative link
 Applying to the Butterfly theme for Hexo
Make sure the APlayer music plugin is enabled before configuring, otherwise the configuration won’t do anything…
Place the Meting.min.js file into the [站点根目录]\source\js folder and edit the theme configuration file _config.butterfly.yml,
Change the CDN link of the meting_js: option to /js/Meting.min.js
# CDN
# Don't modify the following settings unless you know how they work
# 非必要請不要修改
CDN:
  # The CDN provider of internal scripts (主題內部 js 的 cdn 配置)
  # option: local/jsdelivr/unpkg/cdnjs/custom
  # Dev version can only choose. ( dev版的主題只能設置為 local )
  internal_provider: local

  # The CDN provider of third party scripts (第三方 js 的 cdn 配置)
  # option: local/jsdelivr/unpkg/cdnjs/custom
  # when set it to local, you need to install hexo-butterfly-extjs
  third_party_provider: unpkg

  # Add version number to CDN, true or false
  version: false

  # Custom format
  # For example: https://cdn.staticfile.org/${cdnjs_name}/${version}/${min_cdnjs_file}
  custom_format:

  option:
    aplayer_css: https://npm.elemecdn.com/aplayer/dist/APlayer.min.css
    aplayer_js: https://npm.elemecdn.com/aplayer/dist/APlayer.min.js
    meting_js: /js/Meting.min.js
Finally, the usual Hexo three-step combo, of course!
hexo cl; hexo g; hexo s
You can press F12 to check whether the Meting.min.js file has loaded
 Credits

GitHub: xizeyoupan/Meting-API

title: HTTP Status Code Definitions
content:
Status Code
Meaning




100
The client should continue sending the request. This interim response is used to inform the client that part of its request has been received by the server and has not yet been rejected. The client should continue sending the remainder of the request, or, if the request has already been completed, ignore this response. The server must send a final response to the client after the request is completed.


101
The server has understood the client’s request and will notify the client through the Upgrade message header to use a different protocol to complete this request. After sending the final blank line of this response, the server will switch to the protocols defined in the Upgrade header. Similar measures should be taken only when switching to a new protocol is beneficial. For example, switching to a new HTTP version is more advantageous than the old version, or switching to a real-time and synchronous protocol to transmit resources that use such features.


102
A status code extended by WebDAV (RFC 2518), indicating that processing will continue.


200
The request has succeeded, and the response header or data body desired by the request will be returned with this response.


201
The request has been fulfilled, and a new resource has been created as needed by the request, and its URI has been returned with the Location header. If the required resource cannot be created in time, ‘202 Accepted’ should be returned.


202
The server has accepted the request but has not yet processed it. Just as it may be rejected, the request may or may not be executed eventually. In the case of asynchronous operations, there is no more convenient way than sending this status code. The purpose of returning a 202 status code response is to allow the server to accept requests for other processes (for example, a batch-based operation that is executed only once a day) without making the client keep the connection to the server until the batch operation is fully completed. A response that accepts the request for processing and returns 202 should include in the returned entity some information indicating the current processing status, as well as a pointer to a processing status monitor or status prediction, so that the user can estimate whether the operation has been completed.


203
The server has successfully processed the request, but the entity header metainformation returned is not a definitive set valid on the origin server, but comes from a local or third-party copy. The current information may be a subset or superset of the original version. For example, including resource metadata may cause the origin server to know a superset of the metainformation. Using this status code is not required, and it is only appropriate when the response would otherwise return 200 OK.


204
The server successfully processed the request but does not need to return any entity content, and wishes to return updated metainformation. The response may return new or updated metainformation in the form of entity headers. If such header information exists, it should correspond to the requested variables. If the client is a browser, the user’s browser should retain the page that sent the request without making any changes to the document view, even if, according to the specification, the new or updated metainformation should be applied to the document in the user’s browser active view. Because a 204 response is prohibited from containing any message body, it always ends with the first blank line after the message headers.


205
The server successfully processed the request and did not return any content. However, unlike a 204 response, a response returning this status code requires the requester to reset the document view. This response is mainly used to immediately reset a form after accepting user input so that the user can easily start another input. Like a 204 response, this response is also prohibited from containing any message body and ends with the first blank line after the message headers.


206
The server has successfully processed a partial GET request. HTTP download tools such as FlashGet or Thunder use this type of response to implement resumable downloads or to split a large document into multiple download segments for simultaneous download.The request must contain a Range header to indicate the range of content the client wishes to obtain, and may contain If-Range as a request condition.The response must contain the following header fields:Content-Range to indicate the range of content returned in this response; if it is a multipart download with Content-Type multipart/byteranges, each multipart segment should contain a Content-Range field to indicate the content range of that segment. If the response contains Content-Length, its value must match the actual number of bytes of the returned content range. Date, ETag, and/or Content-Location, if the same request should have returned a 200 response. Expires, Cache-Control, and/or Vary, if their values may differ from those of other responses to the same variables. If this response request uses If-Range strong cache validation, then this response should not contain other entity headers; if this response request uses If-Range weak cache validation, then this response is prohibited from containing other entity headers; this avoids inconsistency between the cached entity content and the updated entity header information. Otherwise, this response should contain all entity header fields that should have been returned in a 200 response. If the ETag or Last-Modified header cannot match exactly, the client cache is prohibited from combining the content returned by the 206 response with any previously cached content. Any cache that does not support Range and Content-Range headers is prohibited from caching the content returned by a 206 response.


207
A status code extended by WebDAV (RFC 2518), indicating that the following message body will be an XML message and may contain a series of independent response codes depending on the number of previous subrequests.


300
The requested resource has a series of selectable feedback information, each with its own specific address and browser-driven negotiation information. The user or browser can choose a preferred address for redirection. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response should include an entity with a list of resource characteristics and addresses so that the user or browser can select the most suitable redirect address. The format of this entity is determined by the format defined by Content-Type. The browser may automatically make the most appropriate choice based on the response format and its own capabilities. Of course, the RFC 2616 specification does not specify how such automatic selection should be performed. If the server itself already has a preferred feedback choice, the URI of this feedback should be indicated in Location; the browser may use this Location value as the address for automatic redirection. In addition, unless otherwise specified, this response is also cacheable.


301
The requested resource has been permanently moved to a new location, and any future references to this resource should use one of the URIs returned by this response. If possible, a client with link-editing capabilities should automatically change the requested address to the address returned by the server. Unless otherwise specified, this response is also cacheable. The new permanent URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. If this is not a GET or HEAD request, the browser is prohibited from automatically performing redirection unless the user confirms it, because the conditions of the request may change as a result. Note: For some browsers using HTTP/1.0, if their POST request receives a 301 response, the subsequent redirect request will become a GET request.


302
The requested resource is currently responding to requests from a different URI. Because such a redirect is temporary, the client should continue to send future requests to the original address. This response is cacheable only if specified in Cache-Control or Expires. The new temporary URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. If this is not a GET or HEAD request, the browser is prohibited from automatically performing redirection unless the user confirms it, because the conditions of the request may change as a result. Note: Although RFC 1945 and RFC 2068 do not allow clients to change the request method during redirection, many existing browsers treat a 302 response as a 303 response and use GET to access the URI specified in Location, ignoring the original request method. Status codes 303 and 307 were added to clarify what kind of reaction the server expects from the client.


303
The response corresponding to the current request can be found at another URI, and the client should use GET to access that resource. This method exists mainly to allow the output of a POST request activated by a script to be redirected to a new resource. This new URI is not a substitute reference for the original resource. At the same time, a 303 response is prohibited from being cached. Of course, the second request (the redirect) may be cached. The new URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. Note: Many browsers before HTTP/1.1 cannot correctly understand the 303 status. If interaction with these browsers needs to be considered, the 302 status code should be sufficient, because most browsers handle 302 responses in exactly the way the above specification requires clients to handle 303 responses.


304
If the client sent a conditional GET request and the request has been allowed, and the content of the document (since the last access or according to the request conditions) has not changed, the server should return this status code. A 304 response is prohibited from containing a message body, so it always ends with the first blank line after the message headers.The response must contain the following header information:Date, unless the server has no clock. If a server without a clock also follows these rules, then proxy servers and clients can add the Date field to the received response headers themselves (as specified in RFC 2068), and the caching mechanism will work normally.ETag and/or Content-Location, if the same request should have returned a 200 response.Expires, Cache-Control, and/or Vary, if their values may differ from those of other responses to the same variables.If this response request uses strong cache validation, then this response should not contain other entity headers; otherwise (for example, a conditional GET request uses weak cache validation), this response is prohibited from containing other entity headers; this avoids inconsistency between the cached entity content and the updated entity header information.If a 304 response indicates that a current entity is not cached, the cache system must ignore this response and repeatedly send a request without restrictions.If a 304 response requiring an update to a cache entry is received, the cache system must update the entire entry to reflect the values of all fields updated in the response.


305
The requested resource must be accessed through the specified proxy. The Location field will give the URI information of the specified proxy, and the recipient needs to send a separate request again to access the corresponding resource through this proxy. Only the origin server can create a 305 response. Note: RFC 2068 does not clarify that a 305 response is for redirecting a single request and can only be created by the origin server. Ignoring these restrictions may lead to serious security consequences.


306
In the latest version of the specification, the 306 status code is no longer used.


307
The requested resource is currently responding to requests from a different URI. Because such a redirect is temporary, the client should continue to send future requests to the original address. This response is cacheable only if specified in Cache-Control or Expires. The new temporary URI should be returned in the Location field of the response. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response entity should contain a hyperlink to the new URI and a brief description. Because some browsers cannot recognize 307 responses, the above necessary information needs to be added so that users can understand and send access requests to the new URI. If this is not a GET or HEAD request, the browser is prohibited from automatically performing redirection unless the user confirms it, because the conditions of the request may change as a result.


400
1. The semantics are incorrect, and the current request cannot be understood by the server. Unless modified, the client should not resubmit this request. 2. The request parameters are incorrect.


401
The current request requires user authentication. This response must contain a WWW-Authenticate information header suitable for the requested resource to ask for user information. The client may resubmit a request containing the appropriate Authorization header information. If the current request already contains Authorization credentials, then the 401 response means that server authentication has rejected those credentials. If the 401 response contains the same authentication challenge as the previous response, and the browser has already attempted authentication at least once, the browser should display the entity information contained in the response to the user, because this entity information may contain relevant diagnostic information. See RFC 2617.


402
This status code is reserved for possible future needs.


403
The server has understood the request but refuses to execute it. Unlike a 401 response, authentication cannot help, and this request should not be resubmitted. If this is not a HEAD request and the server wishes to explain clearly why the request cannot be executed, it should describe the reason for refusal in the entity. Of course, the server may also return a 404 response if it does not want the client to obtain any information.


404
The request failed, and the resource desired by the request was not found on the server. No information can tell the user whether this situation is temporary or permanent. If the server knows the situation, it should use the 410 status code to inform that the old resource has become permanently unavailable due to some internal configuration mechanism problem, and that there is no address to jump to. The 404 status code is widely used when the server does not want to reveal why the request was rejected or when no other suitable response is available.


405
The request method specified in the request line cannot be used for the requested resource. This response must return an Allow header to indicate the list of request methods that the current resource can accept. Given that PUT and DELETE methods perform write operations on server resources, most web servers do not support or do not allow the above request methods under the default configuration, and will return a 405 error for such requests.


406
The content characteristics of the requested resource cannot satisfy the conditions in the request headers, so a response entity cannot be generated. Unless this is a HEAD request, the response should return an entity containing a list of entity characteristics and addresses from which the user or browser can select the most suitable one. The format of the entity is determined by the media type defined in the Content-Type header. The browser can make the best choice on its own based on the format and its own capabilities. However, the specification does not define any standard for making such automatic selection.


407
Similar to a 401 response, except that the client must authenticate on the proxy server. The proxy server must return a Proxy-Authenticate to perform the authentication challenge. The client can return Proxy-Authorization header information for verification. See RFC 2617.


408
Request timeout. The client did not complete sending a request within the time the server was prepared to wait. The client can resubmit this request at any time without any changes.


409
The request cannot be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the requested resource. This code may only be used in situations where the user is considered able to resolve the conflict and will resubmit a new request. The response should contain enough information for the user to discover the source of the conflict. Conflicts usually occur when processing PUT requests. For example, in an environment using version checking, if the version information attached to a PUT request to modify a specific resource conflicts with a previous (third-party) request, then the server should return a 409 error to inform the user that the request cannot be completed. At this time, the response entity is likely to contain a comparison of the differences between the two conflicting versions so that the user can resubmit a new merged version.


410
The requested resource is no longer available on the server, and there is no known forwarding address. Such a situation should be considered permanent. If possible, a client with link-editing capabilities should delete all references to this address after obtaining user permission. If the server does not know or cannot determine whether this situation is permanent, it should use the 404 status code. Unless otherwise specified, this response is cacheable. The purpose of the 410 response is mainly to help website administrators maintain the website, notify users that the resource is no longer available, and that the server owner hopes that all remote links pointing to this resource will also be deleted. Such events are common in limited-time, value-added services. Likewise, the 410 response is also used to notify the client that on the current server site, a resource that originally belonged to an individual is no longer available. Of course, whether all permanently unavailable resources need to be marked as ‘410 Gone’, and how long this mark needs to be kept, depends entirely on the server owner.


411
The server refuses to accept the request without a defined Content-Length header. After adding a valid Content-Length header indicating the length of the request message body, the client can submit the request again.


412
The server failed to satisfy one or more of the preconditions given in the request header fields during verification. This status code allows the client to set preconditions in the request metainformation (request header field data) when obtaining a resource, thereby preventing the request method from being applied to resources other than the desired content.


413
The server refuses to process the current request because the size of the entity data submitted by the request exceeds the range the server is willing or able to process. In this case, the server may close the connection to prevent the client from continuing to send this request. If this situation is temporary, the server should return a Retry-After response header to inform the client how long to wait before retrying.


414
The length of the requested URI exceeds the length the server can interpret, so the server refuses to service the request. This is relatively rare. Common cases include: a form submission that should have used POST becomes a GET method, causing the query string to be too long. Redirect URI ‘black holes’, for example, each redirect includes the old URI as part of the new URI, causing the URI to become too long after several redirects. The client is attempting to exploit a security vulnerability in some servers to attack the server. Such servers use fixed-length buffers to read or operate on the requested URI. When the parameters after GET exceed a certain value, a buffer overflow may occur, causing arbitrary code execution[1]. Servers without such vulnerabilities should return the 414 status code.


415
For the method of the current request and the requested resource, the entity submitted in the request is not in a format supported by the server, so the request is rejected.


416
If the request contains a Range request header, and any data range specified in Range does not overlap with the available range of the current resource, and the request does not define an If-Range request header, then the server should return the 416 status code. If Range uses byte ranges, then this situation means that the first byte position of all data ranges specified in the request exceeds the length of the current resource. The server should also include a Content-Range entity header when returning the 416 status code to indicate the length of the current resource. This response is also prohibited from using multipart/byteranges as its Content-Type.


417
The expectation specified in the Expect request header cannot be satisfied by the server, or the server is a proxy server and has clear evidence that the content of Expect cannot be satisfied at the next node on the current route.


421
The number of connections from the IP address where the current client is located to the server exceeds the maximum range permitted by the server. Usually, the IP address here refers to the client address seen from the server (such as the user’s gateway or proxy server address). In this case, the calculation of the number of connections may involve more than one end user.


422
The number of connections from the IP address where the current client is located to the server exceeds the maximum range permitted by the server. Usually, the IP address here refers to the client address seen from the server (such as the user’s gateway or proxy server address). In this case, the calculation of the number of connections may involve more than one end user.


422
The request format is correct, but it cannot be responded to because it contains semantic errors. (RFC 4918 WebDAV) 423 Locked The current resource is locked. (RFC 4918 WebDAV)


424
The current request failed due to an error in a previous request, for example PROPPATCH. (RFC 4918 WebDAV)


425
Defined in the WebDav Advanced Collections draft, but not present in the WebDAV Ordered Collections Protocol (RFC 3658).


426
The client should switch to TLS/1.0. (RFC 2817)


449
A Microsoft extension, indicating that the request should be retried after appropriate operations have been performed.


500
The server encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from completing the processing of the request. Generally, this problem occurs when there is an error in the server’s program code.


501
The server does not support a certain function required by the current request. When the server cannot recognize the request method and cannot support its requests for any resource.


502
The server acting as a gateway or proxy received an invalid response from the upstream server while attempting to execute the request.


503
Due to temporary server maintenance or overload, the server is currently unable to process the request. This situation is temporary and will recover after a period of time. If the delay time can be estimated, the response may contain a Retry-After header to indicate this delay time. If this Retry-After information is not given, the client should handle it in the same way as a 500 response. Note: The existence of the 503 status code does not mean that the server must use it when overloaded. Some servers simply wish to refuse client connections.


504
The server acting as a gateway or proxy did not receive a timely response from the upstream server (the server identified by the URI, such as HTTP, FTP, LDAP) or an auxiliary server (such as DNS) while attempting to execute the request. Note: Some proxy servers return 400 or 500 errors when DNS queries time out.


505
The server does not support, or refuses to support, the HTTP version used in the request. This implies that the server cannot or is unwilling to use the same version as the client. The response should contain an entity describing why the version is not supported and which protocols the server supports.


506
Extended by the Transparent Content Negotiation Protocol (RFC 2295), indicating that the server has an internal configuration error: the requested negotiated variant resource is configured to use itself in transparent content negotiation, and therefore is not a suitable focus in a negotiation process.


507
The server cannot store the content necessary to complete the request. This situation is considered temporary. WebDAV (RFC 4918)


509
The server has reached its bandwidth limit. This is not an official status code, but it is still widely used.


510
The policy required to obtain the resource has not been satisfied. (RFC 2774)



(This is part 1 of 2 of the same post.)

HTTP 状态码 - 维基百科

Recommended Tools for Adjusting Monitor Screen Brightness
content:
Most monitors require you to press buttons on the back to adjust brightness, and since it’s easy to forget which button controls brightness, you often end up hitting the wrong one—such a hassle!
So I went to the world’s largest sex community platform and found this Monitorian brightness-adjustment utility to replace the buttons. It makes adjusting brightness much more convenient, and the interface is somewhat similar to laptop brightness controls.

Microsoft Store 版本 offers more settings and features, such as hotkey support.
 Requirements

Windows 7 or later
.NET Framework 4.8 runtime
DDC/CI must be enabled on the monitor; it’s usually enabled by default on modern displays

 Credits

GitHub: emoacht/Monitorian

title: Carousel Plugin Beautification Based on the Butterfly Theme
Resolving the spawn failed error when pushing with Hexo
content:
Reproducing the Problem
Reproducing this problem is easy. It’s most likely a network issue: just turn off your proxy tool, accelerator, or similar network-optimization software, then make sure the pushing device’s network is within mainland China, and chances are you’ll reproduce it…

 Solving the Problem
These problems are usually caused by an unstable network environment, so start with the network. First, use a network proxy tool to relay the current device’s network environment—relay the resources Hexo pushes to another device, and send them to GitHub from that device.
 0x0001
I personally use Clash as the proxy medium; check the proxy port.

Note down this port 7890. If you’re using v2ray proxy, the default port is usually 1080.
 0x0002
Use the following command in the terminal to change git's global proxy settings
git config --global http.proxy http://127.0.0.1:7890
--global means global, 127.0.0.1 means the local machine, and 7890 refers to the proxy port you noted down earlier.
 0x0003
Change the push address to an https address. You can go to your GitHub repository, click “Code>HTTPS” and copy it.

Then edit the _config.yml configuration file in your Hexo site’s root directory to change the push address.

If you were already using an https address rather than ssh, you can skip this step.
 0x0004
Then it’s the Hexo trio! Check whether the push succeeded.
hexo cl && hexo g && hexo d
Don’t forget to enable your proxy tool.

title: Twikoo Comment System Backup and Modify Data
content:
Exporting Comment Data
 Method 1
You can go to the 管理面板 of the comments in Twikoo, select the 导出 tab, and click the 导出评论 button to export Twikoo’s comment data into a json file.

 Method 2 (Recommended)
Export the comment data of Twikoo into a json file. For details, see the following article:

Twikoo 评论数据导出教程 - iMaeGoo’s Blog

 Restoring Comment Data
If you only want to back up the data and have no other needs, you’re done at this step. To restore comment data later, simply select the 导入 tab, choose the source system Twikoo（JSON）, select the backup file you exported, and click 开始导入. If you also need to modify the comment data, keep reading.
 Editing Comment Data
You can open the Twikoo comment data file with the .json extension using Visual Studio Code or another IDE to edit the comment data you see. You can refer to the table below for the meaning of common fields when making changes:



Value
Meaning




nick
Nickname


mail
Email


mailMd5
Email MD5 value


link
Website link


ua
Device user agent code


ip
IP address


master
Whether the commenter is the site owner


url
Relative path from the homepage


href
Absolute path of the current location when the comment was sent


comment
Comment content


isSpam
Whether it is spam


created
Creation timestamp


updated
Update timestamp


avatar
Avatar link


top
Whether it is pinned




After editing, go to the database of your Twikoo comments—for example, my MongoDB Cloud—and delete the comment item.

Of course, you can use a better method as long as the comment item is eventually deleted…
Once you’ve finished deleting, follow the above Restoring Comment Data steps and the modification is complete.

title: Double 11 Impulse Purchase: Kioxia RC20 SSD Experience
content:
Why I Bought It
Hahaha! The crappy DRAM-less, non-in-house-NAND SSD “威刚 XPG S11 Lite 1T” that had been tormenting me for over half a year is finally replaced! I’d originally planned to wait for 铠侠 RC20 2T during JD’s Double 11 this year, when it would drop to its all-time low for the second time and then buy it. Unfortunately, SSD prices haven’t come back down yet. If I’d known, I would’ve just bought it during 618 this year and wouldn’t be losing 80+ yuan now… Plus the old SSD couldn’t hold on, and it actually gave out first… Recently, drive dropouts, blue screens, crashes, and data loss have been happening frequently, which greatly affected my daily use and was really frustrating. So when the price was still 80+ yuan above the all-time low, I finally couldn’t resist and bought 铠侠 RC20 2T! And that’s how this article came about. Needless to say, the past half year of use before the replacement was miserable—0E throwing errors and losing data every day was a real pain…
 The Old Drive
Over three thousand 0E is truly outrageous… even fiercer than Samsung!

It comes with a built-in heatsink shroud, single-sided chip design, and the overall looks are decent—but looks are all it has. Because of the single-sided design, it’s a bit thinner than those with chips on both sides…


 Unboxing the New Drive
JD offers 30-day price protection and 7-day no-reason returns, and I stacked a few coupons on top—not bad, though the price… well, you know how it is.

The outer packaging is standard, nothing flashy.


Because it’s single-sided, it’s fairly thin, which is nice—if you’re not worried about heat, you can even add a copper heatsink and install it in a laptop…


I have way too much software and study material data, and I couldn’t be bothered to reinstall the system, so I just used DiskGenius to migrate the data from the old SSD, then did an over-the-top install of the system to fill in the missing files. Woohoo~


 Basic Specs
It’s been a while since I bought the new SSD from JD. After all, it’s an entry-level drive with in-house TLC NAND, a Pcie3.0 mid-speed SSD, and the overall experience is fine—at least it has a cache. Due to the “1,000 on the drive = 1,024 in the system” issue, the actual capacity is a bit less than the rated capacity. I bought the 2TB version, and it actually shows 1.81TB.





 SSD Testing
Overall it’s fine. I’ll see after using it for a while whether it 0E. That said, RC20 failures seem pretty rare—most failures are caused by the user’s own doing… MB/s 每秒传输速度 is standard, iops 每秒读写次数 is okay, and the file benchmark 100GB performs fine, matching mid-speed Pcie3.0. After all, I don’t have a need to copy large files 24/7; stability is my top priority. Game loading generally depends on 4K随机读写 fragmented files and doesn’t care much about an SSD’s peak speed. Under normal circumstances, the gap between entry-level and top-tier SSDs is less than 2s, so personally I don’t think it’s necessary to spend more money on Pcie4.0. Stability, no data loss, and no 0E errors come first. After all, Kioxia’s predecessor is Toshiba, so stability and compatibility are pretty good… Why not buy a bulk-shipped MLC drive whose endurance crushes TLC? Heh, it’s been hammered by enterprises for so long—even if the NAND isn’t dead, the controller is on its last legs, and bulk-shipped goods have no official warranty. Of course, I can’t speak for anyone’s preferences or tastes, so forget it—I’m going for stability, hehe~~

title: A Record of My Second Lucid Dream Control Experience
content:
Preface
Let me write down my second-ever experience with a lucid dream and dream control that I had a while back…
As for the first lucid dream, it happened many years ago. From what I vaguely remember, I didn’t succeed at dream control that time, and I’ve mostly forgotten the details anyway, so I’ll let it go and not dwell on it. No record for that one…
 Before Sleep
I ** jerked off** once while showering. After I got out, I watched some long videos about a passenger plane crashing after a mid-air disaster and getting ripped off buying a knockoff phone for a while, then went to sleep…
 Posture
My right side was lying on the 丛雨 dakimakura of 1.8m…
 Mindset
Years in advance, I had laid down a mental imprint of wanting to spend my life with a certain someone who is close to my ideal girl in my mind…
 The Process
I don’t remember her face or exactly what she looked like, but I have a rough impression of the clothes she was wearing,
and during the process of disconnecting from the dream world, the brain’s cleanup mechanism caused me to lose that part of the memory…
But I clearly remember that while in the dream, I knew what clothes she was wearing…
I remember that during the dream I also successfully controlled one action in the dream,
That’s right, dream control!
I remember trying several times to issue commands of control to myself in the dream,
and after trying for a while, I finally forcibly intervened and made my dream self hug her,
and I also vaguely remember that she was a flat chest (small breasts)!
That real feeling of bodily contact, which modern technology can’t compare to, was just so awesome!
According to what I still remember, after the hug ended, she took my hand and floated up out of thin air,
and then, with the front of my belly facing the ground, we started spinning in a circular motion, slowly accelerating. The feeling of weightlessness and acceleration grew stronger and stronger,
and as we spun, the connection gradually broke, and eventually I exited the dream world…
 After Waking
For a short while after waking up, I felt an unprecedented excitement, the kind of feeling you get when you’re going through a major life event,
and once I realized I was awake, I sat on the bed and thought for a little while…
It occurred to me that if I didn’t write this down in my notes, then after some time this precious experience would probably be lost forever…
By then I’d really have missed out! At that thought, I picked up the phone I’d left by the bed, opened my notes app, and started temporarily recording the specific details…
After a while, I organized the memories my brain had at the time, cross-validated each detail in the dream, and proofread the notes I’d jotted down temporarily,
and that’s how this article came to be published…
Because this sleep was very short—I woke up in less than an hour—I didn’t experience much stuff in the dream, which is a real shame…

title: After a Thousand Days of Genshin Impact, Finally Reached Full Stars in the Abyss
content:
It’s been a thousand days since I first started Genshin Impact, and I’ve finally managed to comfortably grind out full stars in the Spiral Abyss! It’s been a long time since I first got full stars…
I remember the first time I got full stars, I think I used the character-swapping method—
that is, clear floors 1 and 2 with a good team, then quit out,
swap characters for floors 2 and 3, grind through floors 1 and 2 with a relatively weaker team, and then retry floors 2 and 3.

Back to this full-star run,
on the final floor 12, that lava monster was pure torture!
To leave a full minute and a half for the second half, I restarted there several times.
That thing kept burrowing around, so I always whiffed my bursts—absolute misery.
Every attempt I’d miss full stars by just a few seconds, which put me in a foul mood, and my performance got worse each time.
It might also be because I play pretty casually, so I don’t have much skill.
Midway through the Abyss I got so mad I cursed out loud: “Damn you, miHoYo number-crunching actuaries!”
After a long stretch of painful fighting, I finally left over a minute for the second half.
And when I fought the water monster at the end, I managed to hit full stars with just seconds to spare before the seven-minute mark.
I have to say, Raiden’s buff really is satisfying! It’s just that I pulled her recently and haven’t built her much, so her potential isn’t fully realized.

Having played Genshin for so long, it’s about time I started thinking about quitting or going casual.
Because this game takes up too much time and is too grindy—so much that it’s affecting my daily life.
Taking a break for a while doesn’t work either; you lose a huge amount of resources for when you come back, and playing feels like more effort than it’s worth.
Same with artifacts—the drop rates are so deliberately low that miHoYo’s number-crunching actuaries clearly have their hands in it.
The more I think about it, the more pointless it feels, and the same thought keeps popping into my head: “Am I playing the game, or is the game playing me?”
After all, miHoYo itself said: play if you like it, and don’t force yourself if you don’t—it’s a two-way choice.
So maybe in the near future… the red thread connecting me and this game for a thousand days will be cut.
When I pick up new games in the future, I’ll probably think a bit more carefully—
at least about whether it’s actually a game, and not some organization’s experiment using the public as lab rats.

title: Common Commands and Configuration Files for Updating the Reflector Mirror List
content:
Reflector is a Python script; it fetches the latest mirror list from the Arch Linux Mirror Status page, filters out the newest mirrors and sorts them by speed, then writes the results to the /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist file.
Here I’ve documented my commonly used commands and configuration files for reflector.
 Commands
reflector --country China --latest 5 --sort rate --save /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist

 Configuration
--save /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist
--country China
--latest 5
--sort rate

Filter out the 5 newest mirrors located in China and sort them by speed, then write the results to the /etc/pacman.d/mirrorlist file.

Hugo Chinese Reading Time Calculation Template
content:
Recently, while hand-building some curious “小” website, I noticed that the ReadingTime method built into the Hugo generator — which returns the estimated reading time for a given page — isn’t very accurate for CJK languages. So I used the Plain method to get the rendered content of a given page, stripped out all the HTML tags, then used the strings.RuneCount function to get the character count of the given string, and divided that by 60 and 2 to get the reading time in minutes — in other words, reading two characters per second.

title: How to Use Your Own Video as a Dynamic Wallpaper on macOS Tahoe (Aerial Replacement Method)
content:
Turning your own videos into macOS Tahoe dynamic wallpapers is actually a rather quiet little process.
The folder path is
~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.wallpaper/aerials/videos/
Inside there are usually just one or two .mov files, like
4C108785-A7BA-422E-9C79-B0129F1D5550.mov (the kind that’s around 445MB).
The steps go like this:

First go to “System Settings > Wallpaper” and download a Tahoe Aerial dynamic wallpaper so the folder has something in it.
Back up the original .mov file somewhere else (very important).
If your video is webm, convert it to mov with ffmpeg (visually near-lossless):

ffmpeg -i input.webm -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -preset slow -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac -b:a 192k output.mov
Or the more “Apple-flavored” ProRes:
ffmpeg -i input.webm -c:v prores_ks -profile:v 3 -c:a pcm_s16le output.mov

Rename the converted file to exactly the same name as the original (e.g. 4C108785-… .mov).
Replace it in.
Go back to wallpaper settings and pick the Aerial you replaced — you should see your video moving on the lock screen and occasionally on the desktop.

The desktop usually only plays a short segment (to save power), and it moves again when you unlock or switch spaces. The lock screen loops more fully.
If you get a black screen, check whether the exported mov plays properly in QuickTime. H.264 + AAC is the most reliable.
Take your time, no rush… if you break something, just restore the backup.
The feeling of tweaking wallpapers late at night is actually quite gentle, like giving your screen a breath of your own.

This is the wallpaper I use~

title: Creating a Swap File
content:
Okay~ Creating a 4GB swap file for your Debian is easy~ Let’s go step by step:
# 1. 创建 4GB 的 swap 文件（用 fallocate 更快）
sudo fallocate -l 4G /swapfile

# 如果 fallocate 不可用，就用 dd（比较慢）
# sudo dd if=/dev/zero of=/swapfile bs=1M count=4096 status=progress

# 2. 设置权限（很重要！）
sudo chmod 600 /swapfile

# 3. 设置为 swap 格式
sudo mkswap /swapfile

# 4. 立即启用
sudo swapon /swapfile

# 5. 开机自动挂载（编辑 /etc/fstab）
echo '/swapfile none swap sw 0 0' | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab

# 6. 检查一下～
swapon --show
free -h
All done~ You should have 4GB of swap now~ Want me to help you check how it’s working? ♡

title: Next.js Rendering Mode Troubleshooting Notes: force-dynamic, hydration, and No Database at Build Time
AI Can Write Features but Not Dockerfiles: Next.js Self-Hosting Pitfall Notes
content:
Official docs referenced in this post: Next.js 自托管, Serwist, PM2 配置项, postgres 镜像说明

I’ve been self-hosting three or four Next.js projects back to back lately, so here’s a record of a few pitfalls I hit. Claude writes features amazingly fast — pages, tRPC routes, Prisma schemas all churned out in one go and they just run. But the moment deployment and wrap-up come around, it’s back and forth, the same file edited over and over. Everything below is the “build passes but it won’t run” category, with zero warning signs locally…
Enough chatter — let’s get to it!
 The standalone multi-stage image: only one of these was a real pitfall
I originally wanted to title this “four pitfalls,” but the git log slapped me in the face~ Over its entire lifetime, the Dockerfile in vns-next has only been touched by 4 commits: 404a769 created it, then 0b7117c, 037ccf4, and fefd366 each changed it once. And three of the items below were already written correctly in the very first commit — I never actually “hit” them.
First, the one I actually hit. The build base in 404a769 was originally a plain oven/bun image, and it died outright, so 0b7117c added node:
# 注意：不能用纯 oven/bun 镜像——prisma/next 的 CLI shebang 是 #!/usr/bin/env node，
# 构建环境需要 node；bun 只作为包管理器/脚本运行时拷入
ARG REGISTRY_MIRROR=docker.io
FROM ${REGISTRY_MIRROR}/oven/bun:1 AS bun-dist
FROM ${REGISTRY_MIRROR}/library/node:24-bookworm-slim AS builder
COPY --from=bun-dist /usr/local/bin/bun /usr/local/bin/bun
The oven/bun:1 image has no node at all, so prisma generate dies the moment it runs — but the error only says the CLI can’t find an interpreter, and without looking at the shebang you’d never guess why. The fix: use node:24-bookworm-slim as the base and just COPY a single binary out of the bun image as the package manager.
The other three were already in place in the first commit. Here are a few key excerpts (the original file has no numbering; I’ve split them up for posting):
# Dockerfile:23-24 —— prisma.config.ts 里那句 if (!url) throw 是无条件抛错的，
# 而 generate 根本不连库，所以构建期得塞个占位值
ENV SKIP_ENV_VALIDATION=1
ENV DATABASE_URL="postgresql://build:build@localhost:5432/build"
# Dockerfile:26-28 —— NEXT_PUBLIC_* 在构建期内联进客户端 bundle，
# 改站点域名必须重新 build，所以要走 ARG 而不是运行时环境变量
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://example.com
ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=${NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL}
# Dockerfile:49 —— standalone 的文件追踪可能漏拷 Prisma 生成的客户端资产（含 wasm/schema）
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/src/generated ./src/generated
I think the NEXT_PUBLIC_* one is the easiest to overlook: it’s not a runtime variable, it gets inlined as a literal into the client bundle at the moment of next build. I deliberately wrote it out again in deploy/README.md:153-154 — change a variable like this and you must --build and rebuild the image; editing .env and restarting the container does nothing.
The second real pitfall came at b07e20d: there’s no database container inside the builder layer, and Next by default statically prerenders DB-querying pages during next build, so it’s guaranteed to throw. That one belongs to the rendering mode rather than the image itself, and I covered both the fix and how to verify it in another post; here I’ll just note what it means for the Dockerfile — it’s the only pitfall where “not a single word of the Dockerfile is wrong but the build still won’t pass,” and you can stare at the multi-stage build all day without finding a problem.
 On the compose side: two round trips on registries, ports narrowing all the way down
The registry thing is pretty funny. 037ccf4 swapped all the base images to a domestic mirror + npmmirror, and 12 minutes later fefd366 rolled it back, with the reason in the message: the daemon proxy on the production machine had been fixed, and that mirror didn’t have a oven/bun image anyway. What a mess — after all that circling, only the npmmirror half survived, i.e. the ENV NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY line in Dockerfile:16. Before you swap out infrastructure, check that the other side actually has the image you want…
The compose side converged pretty aggressively. The db service maps no ports at all; data imports and maintenance all go through docker compose exec -T db psql/pg_restore's stdin pipe:
db:
  volumes:
    # postgres:18 官方镜像的卷挂载点改为 /var/lib/postgresql（内含 18/docker 数据目录）
    - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql
  # 不映射任何端口：整机只暴露 app 的 1270 给 Cloudflare Tunnel
The only outward-facing opening is the app service, and it’s pinned to the loopback:
app:
  ports:
    # 只绑本机回环，公网入口走 Cloudflare Tunnel
    - "127.0.0.1:1270:3000"
The volume mount point for postgres:18 changed recently; if you copy it from an older version, your /var/lib/postgresql/data will break. And while I’m complaining: after 0b7117c removed the db port mapping, lines 43, 118, 122, and 126 of deploy/README.md still have the old port numbers — the config and docs no longer match, and AI won’t proactively sync that kind of inconsistency for you…
 The two that don’t use Docker
Not every project is worth bringing compose to. acgn-flow uses PM2, with a single ecosystem.config.cjs config:
instances: 1,
exec_mode: "fork",          // 单实例 fork，不用 cluster
max_memory_restart: "2G",
exp_backoff_restart_delay: 500,
max_restarts: 15,
min_uptime: "30s",
kill_timeout: 5000,
The deploy script is a single line: pnpm build && pm2 reload ecosystem.config.cjs --update-env. Why fork instead of cluster isn’t actually explained in the repo; here’s what I was thinking at the time: Next already does single-process multiplexing, so wrapping another layer of cluster brings little benefit and doubles memory first — but that’s just my judgment, I never actually benchmarked it.
thdl goes the systemd route and has no deploy script — thdl/README.md:64-66 is just three hand-typed rsync commands (.next/standalone/, .next/static, public), retyped every time. A few hardening directives were added to the unit:
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=strict
ProtectHome=true
PrivateTmp=true
ReadWritePaths=/var/www/thdl /var/log/thdl
Of the three, the Dockerfile is the most error-prone: models often mix up what exists in which layer of a multi-stage build — the bun image having no node above is a textbook case. The PM2 one was right on the first try; after all, it has few fields and plain semantics, so it’s hard to get wrong even if you tried.
 Service Workers are the most crash-prone part of self-hosting
I’m giving this its own section because the problems never show up locally.
(This is part 1 of 2 of the same post.)



Project
Problem
Solution




bbps
@serwist/next never worked under pure static export (the reason isn’t in the commit)
c2e3cf48 was introduced, then a commit and over an hour later dd40bcf5 was removed entirely, replaced by a standalone script that runs after the build


bbps
The precache glob also swallowed the hosting platform’s _worker.js
ea65e4b0 changed just 1 line: add '_worker.js' to globIgnores


acgn-flow
Compatibility issues between the official plugin and the bundler
21e3e75 switched to the serwist CLI instead of @serwist/next


acg-site
Some embedded WebViews cache stale pages, causing a blank screen
Skip SW registration and actively unregister any old SW already installed


home
After the PWA was removed, returning visitors still had the old SW
Leave a tombstone SW that unregisters itself (I posted the full implementation in the migration article)



One thing to add about the first row: the commit message for dd40bcf5 only says “removing ‘@serwist/next’ integration”, with no reason given, and neither the README nor the config leaves any explanation. The project is indeed output: 'export' (next.config.ts:4), so I’d guess the two are incompatible, but that’s my inference, not something you can verify in the repo — compare that to the acgn-flow row, where 21e3e75's “fix Turbopack compatibility issue” is written in black and white. The bbps row has nothing.
After the bbps rework, the build became a three-stage chain: next build && node scripts/build-sw.mjs && node scripts/generate-feed.mjs. The middle script first uses esbuild to bundle src/app/sw.ts into a single bundle, then uses injectManifest to scan out/ and inject the precache manifest, and finally unlinkSync deletes the intermediate artifacts. The order can’t be reversed, because out/ is exactly what it globs.
The acg-site one is the most typical; the comment sits right there in src/components/providers.tsx:62-65: that WebView’s caching policy doesn’t match the browser’s, so it easily caches stale pages and causes a blank screen; and you have to unregister proactively, otherwise a user who opened the web version first already has the old SW installed, and going into the WebView still hits the same problem. In the same file, :36-55 also wires up isChunkLoadError() + safeReload(), with a 10-second throttle and sessionStorage deduplication, specifically to rescue the case where old pages can’t load new chunks after a release.
SW bugs never show up locally; they only show up in production, where returning visitors exist…
 The grunt work of moving static assets and the feed around
bbps's RSS isn’t generated by the framework; a standalone Node script writes feed.xml into out/ after the build finishes. The side effect is that the .mjs script can’t import TS modules, so frontmatter parsing is implemented twice, once in scripts/generate-feed.mjs and once in src/lib/blog.tsx:112-123, with nearly line-for-line identical logic — knowing it’s duplicated doesn’t buy you much unless you add another layer of build on top.
Another team project has similar grunt work: after a standalone build you still have to manually copy public and .next/static into the standalone directory, and that logic is written twice — in postbuild and in the deploy script. If the two ever fall out of sync, the symptom is that all styling disappears in production while the build stays green the whole way.
There’s a more insidious one too: files uploaded at runtime by that project were initially written under public, and every standalone rebuild wipes it out, so anything users uploaded was gone after a single release. In the end we moved it to a separate directory and added a read route with path-traversal protection. The same fix also turned up that the URL check in the validation rules rejected site-relative paths — the upload succeeded but couldn’t be saved to the database. Two bugs stacked together took ages to track down.

While writing this I went back and re-checked all the line numbers and commits mentioned above, and it turned out three of the “four pitfalls” I’d originally written down were me wrongly blaming the AI, so I had to delete that section and rewrite it.

Anyway, I’m outta here~

title: In the Same Month, I Moved My Homepage Out of Next.js and Moved a Hugo Site In
content:
In the same month I did two completely opposite things — I moved my personal homepage off Next.js to Vite, and then moved a whole Hugo static site into Next.js… I hit snags on both sides, so let me write them down while I still remember, so I don’t forget again next time~
 The one I moved out
home is my personal homepage repo. The stack’s evolution went like this:



commit
date
event




——
——
Nuxt 4 / Vue 3 / Pinia


412b258
2026-04-21 03:46
Rewritten as Next.js 15 static export, new code in next-app/, public shares with Nuxt via symlink


0e83f8c
2026-04-21 14:12
Nuxt retired, Next project flattened to the root directory


081e5b4
2026-04-21 14:43
Upgraded to Next 16 + Tailwind 4 + TypeScript 6


3075556
2026-05-14 07:50
Migrated to Vite 7



The timing is pretty funny: only 31 minutes between retiring Nuxt and upgrading to Next 16 — two big moves in the same session; and then 22 days later I overturned one of them… impulse is the devil.
Before moving to Vite I did a count:
# 1. src 下所有 tsx
find src -name "*.tsx" | wc -l          # 20
# 2. 其中带 use client 的
grep -rl "use client" src --include="*.tsx" | wc -l   # 19
20 tsx files, 19 of them starting with "use client"… The only Server Component was src/app/layout.tsx — it exported metadata and viewport, wired up Inter via next/font, mounted three preconnect, rendered the html/body shell and the Toaster — it did a lot, but none of it required RSC.
Now look at output: 'export'. This site had been a static export since Next 15; before the move, next.config.ts looked like this:
import type { NextConfig } from "next";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { dirname } from "node:path";

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
  output: "export",
  reactStrictMode: true,
  trailingSlash: false,
  images: { unoptimized: true },
  turbopack: {
    root: dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)),
  },
};

export default nextConfig;
With that choice, SSR / ISR / Route Handler / middleware / next/image optimization were all off, leaving just file routing, the Metadata API, and next/font. For a single-page homepage: routing is useless, meta can just be hardcoded in index.html, and swapping the font for a system stack is something nobody would notice… so why keep it at all?
 The ledger after the migration
The stat for 3075556 was 41 files changed, 902 insertions(+), 1862 deletions(-) — a net reduction of 960 lines.
The config comparison is more telling. What got deleted was next.config.ts(15) + src/app/layout.tsx(69) + next-env.d.ts(6) + serwist.config.js(18), 108 lines total; what I got in return was index.html(45) + src/main.tsx(23) + vite.config.ts(30), 98 lines total. About the same line count, but I can understand the latter at a glance.
Most component diffs were just deleting those two lines at the top:
--- a/src/components/app-footer.tsx
+++ b/src/components/app-footer.tsx
@@ -1,5 +1,3 @@
-"use client";
-
 import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
At that point vite.config.ts was 30 lines; later I trimmed it down to just 14:
import { defineConfig } from "vite";
import react from "@vitejs/plugin-react";
import tsconfigPaths from "vite-tsconfig-paths";

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [react(), tsconfigPaths()],
  server: {
    port: 3000,
  },
  build: {
    target: "es2022",
    sourcemap: false,
  },
});
The clearest illustration is the runtime stage of Dockerfile:
FROM node:22-alpine
RUN npm install -g serve
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./public
EXPOSE 12445
CMD ["serve", "public", "-l", "12445"]
Not even Node has to run — just a static file sitting there, the runtime stage is almost boringly clean…
 A causal chain I cut along the way
The font chain spans two commits. In the Vite migration commit (3075556), Inter in next/font/google was no longer usable, so I swapped in a local @fontsource package, which suddenly added about 5MB of woff2 for Chinese fonts; ten minutes later in ae004b3 it hit me — the main reason I’d installed PWA in the first place was to cache those 5MB, so I might as well switch to a system font stack (PingFang / YaHei / Roboto), and deleted @fontsource along with the PWA.
“Deleted” isn’t quite accurate though… digging through the log, I found the PWA had already been deleted once back in 5321a54, then reinstalled later — this was the second deletion. So this wasn’t some clean decision at all; it took two rounds of back-and-forth before it settled down.
And deleting a PWA isn’t just deleting code. Old visitors still have the old Service Worker in their browsers, so I had to leave a tombstone SW to let it unregister itself:
// Tombstone service worker.
self.addEventListener("install", () => self.skipWaiting());

self.addEventListener("activate", (event) => {
  event.waitUntil(
    (async () => {
      const names = await caches.keys();
      await Promise.all(names.map((n) => caches.delete(n)));
      await self.registration.unregister();
      const clients = await self.clients.matchAll({ type: "window" });
      for (const client of clients) client.navigate(client.url);
    })(),
  );
});
Clear the cache, unregister, then have already-open pages navigate again… removing a feature is way more hassle than removing code.
 The unfinished wrap-up
Then comes the not-so-glorious part. As of today:

README.md still says Next.js 15 + Serwist + Tailwind 3 + NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, but it’s actually Vite 7 + Tailwind 4 + VITE_ — every technical description is wrong
.github/workflows/build.yml:53's artifact is path: out, while Vite output lives in dist, so whatever CI uploads has long been empty
The CSS path in components.json points to src/app/globals.css, but the file moved to src/globals.css ages ago
app-footer.tsx:38's suppressHydrationWarning is dead code — there’s no hydration at all anymore

The funniest part is that 0e83f8c, the time I took Nuxt offline, the commit body actually listed a complete “5 things you have to change along with the framework swap”: Dockerfile, vercel.json, GitHub Actions artifact path, .dockerignore, README… The checklist wasn’t wrong by a single word — the next migration just didn’t follow it, and I didn’t bother to look either.
One more: while cleaning up for e6b5d81 I found @radix-ui/react-slot and class-variance-authority, two dependencies installed by the shadcn scaffold — installed 4-21, deleted 5-14, zero imports across 23 days (there’s no button.tsx in the project at all); .vscode still recommends Vue.volar, leftovers from two frameworks ago. Adding a dependency takes a second; deleting one takes three weeks…
 The one that moved in
On the other side is vns, a Galgame resource site. In the same repo you can see the full three-stage evolution: the old branch is Hexo 8.1.1 + NexT, dev/beast is Hugo Extended, and over on vns, the dev server in .claude/launch.json points straight at the neighboring vns-next directory running bun run dev — two repos migrating side by side for comparison.
There were three reasons to move it into Next.js.
First, a static site has no server, so API keys can only sit in plaintext in the frontend JS. At the time, main.js had this One API key just lying there:
const API_URL = "https://example.com/v1/chat/completions";
const API_KEY = "sk-xxxx";  // 就这么明文躺着
That’s the only option for AI features on a pure static site — no choice. The same thing in Next.js can go into a Route Handler and the key stays server-side. Also, remember to rotate any key that has been in a public repo; changing the code doesn’t count…
Second, this site’s “database” is 6 JSON files under data/. Ad slots, friend links, download sources, translation groups — all fake databases read at build time. Changing one row of data meant rebuilding the whole site and re-pushing the deploy branch, and that branch is 27.9MB / 1832 files… all to change one line of JSON.
Third, to create a “dynamic feel” I’d piled up over two thousand lines of client JS. main.js was 2347 lines before splitting, stuffed with swup page transitions, lazy loading, counter animations, localStorage toggles, SSE streaming requests. Later it was split into 8 ES modules and the main file dropped to 613 lines, but the pitfalls along the way were pretty typical (these are all on the dev branch):

4842e804e: after splitting into ES modules, top-level variables like VALINE_CONFIG stayed in the original file. Module top-level scope doesn’t span files, so the comment component never initialized — and it was users who reported it
187ad71b4: a single try/catch wrapped all the inits, so one crash mid-way killed everything after it. Users reported “comments and TOC are both broken” — the TOC was purely collateral damage. Changed to an independent catch per [name, fn]
